title: Apple reveals how Siri AI features work in China – raising privacy questions
excerpt: Apple has revealed how the new Siri AI features will work for users in China. The new AI features will...
content_html:
Apple has revealed how the new Siri AI features will work for users in China. The new AI features will be powered by Alibaba’s Qwen models.

While the iPhone maker is partnering with Google for access to its Gemini models in most countries, the Chinese government requires Apple to instead partner with a local AI company …

Google’s Gemini models are powering the new Siri AI features in most countries. These run either on Apple’s own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers or on Google-provided servers dedicated to Apple, with protections specific to Siri AI users. These include privacy requirements mirroring those applying to PCC servers, ensuring that neither Apple nor Google has any access to user interactions.

In China, however, the law only permits the use of Chinese AI models. This is likely to ensure that the government is able to monitor usage, and it’s therefore unlikely that the same privacy protections will apply.

Reuters reports that Apple published a guide in which it stated that the new features would rely on Alibaba’s Qwen models. The guide is specific to Mac, but the report says that the same model will be used across iPhone, iPad and Vision Pro also.

Apple’s updated Chinese-language guide says users who opt in can use Qwen through ​Siri for more detailed responses to some requests, including analysis of photos and documents. Writing Tools can also draw on the service to create text or images from a description.

There’s a fairly significant clue that privacy protections will not apply in the same way: Reuters says that Mac users will need their own Qwen account and must be signed into it.

content_html_zh:
苹果公司透露了新的 Siri AI 功能将如何为中国用户服务。 新的人工智能功能将由阿里巴巴的 Qwen 模型提供支持。

虽然这家 iPhone 制造商正在与谷歌合作，在大多数国家/地区使用其 Gemini 机型，但中国政府要求苹果公司与当地人工智能公司合作……

谷歌的 Gemini 模型正在为大多数国家的新 Siri AI 功能提供支持。 它们要么在苹果自己的私有云计算（PCC）服务器上运行，要么在谷歌为苹果提供的专用服务器上运行，并为 Siri AI 用户提供特定的保护。 其中包括反映适用于 PCC 服务器的隐私要求，确保 Apple 和 Google 都无法访问用户交互。

然而在中国，法律只允许使用中国的人工智能模型。 这可能会确保政府能够监控使用情况，因此不太可能适用相同的隐私保护措施。

路透社报道称，苹果发布了一份指南，其中表示新功能将依赖阿里巴巴的 Qwen 机型。 该指南特定于 Mac，但报告称同一模型也将用于 iPhone、iPad 和 Vision Pro。

苹果更新的中文指南称，选择加入的用户可以通过 Siri 使用 Qwen，对某些请求进行更详细的响应，包括分析照片和文档。 书写工具还可以利用该服务根据描述创建文本或图像。

有一个相当重要的线索表明隐私保护不会以同样的方式适用：路透社表示，Mac 用户将需要自己的 Qwen 帐户，并且必须登录该帐户。
